question.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.text: Alcohols are weaker acids than water
Acid strength of alcohols decreases in the following $\mathrm{RCH}_2 \mathrm{OH}>\mathrm{R}_2 \mathrm{CHOH}>\mathrm{R}_3 \mathrm{COH}$
Carbon-oxygen bond length in methanol, $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}$ is shorter than that of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length in phenol.

solution.text: The $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length in alcohols is $142 \mathrm{pm}$ and in Phenol it is $136 \mathrm{pm}$. The $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length in phenol is shorter than that in methanol due to the conjugation of unshared pair of electrons on oxygen with the ring, which imparts double bond character to the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond.
